title: 听力模拟测试
goal: 提取四部分中的信息并辨认逻辑与对应关系。

points.label: 提取四部分中的具体信息
辨认态度、逻辑与对应关系

sources.title: 雅思 IELTS Academic：课表
sources.used: 听力模拟测试的课程组合和教学规格

sources.title: IELTS Academic: Listening test format
sources.used: 听力四部分和录音播放次数

body.p: 听力由四部分组成，录音播放一遍。题型分布在不同试卷中可能变化。
本套按课程的题型组合编写，作答限时 30 分钟。选择题为四选一，选两项的题改为从四个组合中选一个。地图题和配对题从所给名称中选择。录音最多用两个声音。课程通过率不换算为考试分数段。

groups.text:
Part 1 — Community print workshop booking
Name: Mara (1) ______
Course: (2) ______ printing
Date: 18 (3) ______
Start time: (4) ______ am
Number of places: (5) ______
Fee per person: £(6) ______
Contact email: mara@(7) ______.co.uk
Bring: an old (8) ______
Collection point: (9) ______ entrance
Payment method: (10) ______
Write ONE WORD AND/OR ONE NUMBER for each answer.

lines.text: Good morning, Riverside Community Centre. How can I help?

Hello. I saw that you run short practical workshops, and I'd like to book places on one of them. My friend and I are both interested in learning a printing technique. Neither of us has done any printing before, so we wanted to check whether your introductory sessions really are suitable for beginners.
They are. The tutor demonstrates each stage and supplies the equipment. I can take the booking now if you've chosen a course. Could I start with your name?
It's Mara Elwood. That's E L W O O D. My first name is M A R A. My friend will come with me, but you can use my details for the booking.
Thank you. There are two introductory printing workshops. The fabric printing course uses blocks on cloth, while the screen printing course concentrates on paper. Which one did you want?
Fabric printing, please. We talked about the screen course too, but my friend would prefer to work with cloth. Could you tell me the date again? I wrote down the eighteenth but forgot the month.

It's the eighteenth of September. The next fabric session after that is in November, but there are still places in September. The doors open at nine and the teaching starts at nine thirty in the morning.
That's convenient. Please reserve two places. We thought about inviting another friend, but she isn't available that weekend. Is the price still twenty-four pounds each?

The standard fee is twenty-four pounds per person, but for this introductory date it's twenty pounds per person. That includes the materials used during the session. There is no separate charge for the printing blocks.
Fine. My email address is mara at linnet dot co dot uk. That's L I double N E T, all one word before the dot. Please send the confirmation there, rather than to my work address.
I've entered that. We provide an apron, but the tutor asks everyone to bring an old shirt as well, since ink can mark clothing. You don't need to bring fabric; there will be enough for the exercises.
I'll let my friend know. Where should we meet the tutor? I've used the main entrance for a meeting before, but I don't know where the workshop room is.

For this session, go to the garden entrance. The tutor collects the group there and takes everyone through to the studio. The main entrance is open for the café, but it isn't the meeting point. Please arrive a little before the teaching starts.
All right. Can I pay by bank transfer? I could do that this afternoon, or I can bring cash on the day if necessary.

For advance bookings we take payment by card over the phone. We don't take a bank transfer for these sessions, and cash is only used for small purchases at the café. Once payment has been processed, the email will include the date, meeting point and the cancellation details. If your friend needs step-free access, let us know in advance and we'll arrange the route to the studio.
Thank you. Card is fine, and I'll check the access details with her before the day. We will read the confirmation together and make sure we know where to leave our coats when we arrive at the centre.

items.why: 姓氏拼写为 Elwood。
Fabric printing 是确认预订的课程。
录音确认日期为 the eighteenth of September。
教学在 nine thirty 开始。
Please reserve two places 确认两人。
本次入门课每人 twenty pounds，标准价不是本次费用。
邮箱域名逐字拼为 L I double N E T。
tutor asks everyone to bring an old shirt，要求携带旧衬衫。
go to the garden entrance 指明集合入口。
advance bookings 使用 card 支付。

groups.text:
Part 2 — Riverside centre grounds
Map: north ↑
┌(11)──│──(12)┐
├(13)──│──(14)┤
└──────│──────┘
Entrance → path; Café: south-east
A north–south path divides west and east; the entrance is at the south end.
Questions 11–14: choose the place at each numbered position. One place is not used.

lines.text: Welcome to the Riverside centre grounds. I'll describe the plan first, then explain the activities taking place here this afternoon. Please look at the map with north at the top. The entrance is at the south end of the central path, and the café is in the south-east corner. The path runs north from the entrance and divides the west side from the east side. Halfway up the west side, directly beside the path, is the pond. It is a shallow feature used for observation, so please stay on the path around its edge. Directly opposite the pond, on the east side of the path, is the seating area. It has benches under a shelter and can be used throughout the afternoon. Continue north along the central path. At its northern end, the building to the west is the glasshouse. It contains plants being raised for later use in the grounds. Across the path, in the north-east position, is the tool store. The store is normally locked, but a volunteer will be there during the tool-care activity. The café is further south, as shown on the plan, and is not one of the four locations I've just described. Now for the activities. The seed sorting group will meet near the glasshouse. Participants will separate clean seeds from their cases and put them into labelled packets. This is a quiet indoor activity and no previous experience is needed. The tool care group meets at the store. A volunteer will show participants how to clean hand tools before they are put away. It does not involve sharpening blades. At the pond, the bird recording group will note the species they can identify from the path. The group is observing birds, not cleaning the water. Finally, plant drawing takes place in the seating area. Paper and pencils are provided, and participants can draw leaves collected by the volunteers. The drawing group will remain under the shelter if there is light rain. If rain becomes heavy, all four groups will move inside the main building. For anyone joining an activity, please collect a name badge from the reception desk before going outside. The badge lets the volunteer know that the registration form has been completed. There is no charge for the badge and it can be returned at the end of the visit. Drinking water is available from the tap beside the café. Cups are available there too, but bringing a reusable bottle will reduce waste. Children must remain with an accompanying adult around the pond and in the glasshouse. Most paths are level, although the route into the store has a small step; ask at reception if an alternative activity space is needed. The glasshouse can become warm, so coats may be left in the lockers next to reception. Please avoid leaving bags on the paths, where they could obstruct other visitors. The activities finish at four, after which the grounds remain open for another hour. Volunteers can answer questions during the session, but please follow the marked paths between the activity spaces. The labels on the map identify places, whereas the activity list identifies what happens at each place. Both the location and the activity may be mentioned more than once in this introduction. The volunteers will be wearing green badges so that they are easy to identify when you reach each activity.

items.why: the building to the west is the glasshouse 说明北端西侧是 glasshouse。
in the north-east position, is the tool store 说明玻璃房对面的东北侧是 tool store。
Halfway up the west side 是 pond。
pond 对面的东侧是 seating area。café 在东南角，不在四个编号位置上。

groups.text: Questions 15–18: choose the activity at each place. One activity is not used.

items.why: seed sorting group 在 glasshouse 附近集合。
tool care group 在 store 集合。
pond 的活动是 bird recording。录音说 not cleaning the water，所以不是 pond cleaning。
plant drawing 在 seating area 进行。

groups.text: Questions 19–20: write NO MORE THAN TWO WORDS for each answer.

items.stem: (19) What should participants collect from reception? ______
items.why: collect a name badge from the reception desk 指明领取物。

groups.text:
Part 3 — Student project discussion
For questions 25–26, choose the pair of statements supported by the discussion.

lines.text: We've got to settle the plan for our project on how people use the university library. I thought we might start by measuring how many books are borrowed, but the tutor's feedback suggests that would miss what people actually do inside the building.

I agree. Let's focus on how students choose a place to work, rather than the number of loans. That gives us a question we can explore with several methods. We should still acknowledge that borrowing is one reason for visiting, but it isn't our main outcome.

For the first stage, I suggested interviewing staff, but I now think student interviews would tell us more about the choices themselves. Staff could explain the building rules, although they may not know why an individual chose a particular desk.

Yes. We should start with students, and keep a short staff conversation as background if time allows. How many interviews are manageable? We discussed four, six, eight and ten. Eight might be too many to transcribe. I think six would give us enough material for this small project.
Six it is. We'll recruit across different courses, not just from our own class. We can't promise that six people represent the whole university, so the report should make that limit clear.

We also need to choose when to observe the study areas. I initially preferred the evening because I thought the building would be quieter. But if we go at lunchtime, we'll see the period when most seats are in use. That will make it easier to compare locations.
Lunchtime sounds better. We can record whether seats are occupied without noting who is sitting there. Let's avoid collecting names or describing individuals in the observation sheet.

Agreed. The tutor also asked us to think about a questionnaire. I see the advantage of reaching more students, but a long form would be difficult to analyse. We could use a short one to check how common the reasons from the interviews are.

That's a useful complement. I don't think we should replace the interviews with it, though. The interview answers could help us write meaningful options for the questionnaire. We must also explain that responses are voluntary.

So the two decisions for our methods are to keep the interviews and use a short questionnaire afterwards. We considered looking at the library's old seating plans, but those won't tell us what current students prefer. We also discussed recording sound levels, but we don't have suitable equipment.

Now, the tutor gave us five possible ways to present the results. I think a chart showing occupied seats by area would make the observation counts clear. A map could show locations too, but we shouldn't put individual interview comments on it.

Let's use the chart and include a small table of interview themes. A long transcript would take too much space, and we don't need a photograph of each desk. We can describe the building briefly in the introduction instead.

We should divide the preparation among the group. I'll ask Nina to prepare the interview questions; she's already drafted a topic list. Omar can design the questionnaire once we have the interview themes.

I'll ask Priya to organise the observation sheet for the seating counts. Then Sam can check the archive for the building's earlier layout, just for background. A laboratory task isn't needed for this project.

Good. We'll review each person's draft together before collecting anything. The observation sheet needs to distinguish the quiet floor from the collaborative area, but both should use the same measure of occupancy. That will make the comparison easier to interpret.

And our final report will separate what people say from what we observe. An occupied seat tells us that someone is using a place; it doesn't tell us why. The interviews can suggest reasons, while the questionnaire can help us see how often those reasons are reported.

items.stem: (21) What is the project's main focus?
options: How staff explain the building rules
How the building's older seating was arranged
items.why: focus on how students choose a place to work 确定项目主题。

items.stem: (22) How many student interviews do they agree to conduct?
items.why: Six it is 确认采访人数为六。

items.stem: (23) Why do they choose lunchtime for observation?
options: It allows staff interviews to replace counts.
It is the quietest period in the building.
It shows a period with many occupied seats.
It avoids the need to compare study areas.
items.why: lunchtime 是 most seats are in use 的时段。

items.stem: (24) What concern does the student express about the questionnaire?
options: A short form would prevent participation.
The form would expose names on the chart.
Its results would replace all observations.
A long form would be difficult to analyse.
items.why: a long form would be difficult to analyse 指明顾虑。

items.stem: (25) Which TWO methods do the students decide to use?
options: Student interviews and a short questionnaire
Old seating plans and sound-level recording
Student interviews and old seating plans
items.why: keep the interviews 和 use a short questionnaire afterwards 是两项决定。

items.stem: (26) Which TWO ways of presenting results do they select?
options: A detailed seating map and a complete interview transcript
A chart of occupied seats and a table of themes
A photograph of each desk and a seating map
A table of themes and a full transcript
items.why: use the chart 和 include a small table of interview themes 是选定的两项。

Priya 负责 organise the observation sheet。

groups.text:
Part 4 — Paper conservation study
Notes: Damage can be caused by (31) ______. The first inspection uses a (32) ______.
Table: sample | treatment | recorded feature
A | dry storage | (33) ______
B | humidified storage | (34) ______
Sentences: The team avoided direct (35) ______ on the paper. A comparison requires a consistent (36) ______.
Flow: inspect → place between (37) ______ → apply light pressure → store in a (38) ______.
Diagram of a storage package, cross-section:
(39) → ┌─outer cover─────┐
│ paper sample │
│ supporting layer ← (40) │
└──────────────────┘
Write ONE WORD from the recording for each answer.

lines.text: Today I'll describe a teaching study in paper conservation. The study concerns sheets kept in a small collection and is designed to compare observations made under two storage arrangements. It does not provide a universal treatment for every document. Paper can be damaged by moisture, among other causes. Repeated handling can also damage fragile edges, so the team arranged its work to minimise unnecessary movement. Before any treatment, the team inspected each sheet with a magnifier. This allowed the observers to record small marks without touching them. They described each sheet and photographed it in the same position. The first set of notes concerned visible features, not assumptions about how the marks had developed. Two samples were then stored under different conditions for the teaching comparison. Sample A was kept in dry storage. For this sample, the team recorded its colour at each inspection. Sample B was kept in humidified storage, and the feature recorded for it was flexibility. The researchers used separate records so that the treatment and the feature would not be confused. They did not claim that humidity was appropriate for every sheet, and they did not expose valuable documents to this demonstration. The sheets were prepared specifically for the class. When the students photographed them, they avoided direct sunlight on the paper. Light from the room was used instead. The same camera position was maintained at each inspection, but the team also understood that photographs alone do not capture every physical property. For a comparison across inspections, the team used a consistent scale beside each sheet. The scale provided a reference for the dimensions in the images. It did not measure the chemical condition of the paper. The handling procedure followed a set sequence. After inspection, the sheet was placed between boards. A light pressure was then applied to keep the sheet flat. The boards were clean and smooth; they were not intended to remove marks from the surface. After this stage, the sheet was stored in a folder. The folder kept the sheet together with its record, while the boards served during the pressing stage. The class also examined a simplified package in cross-section. The outer cover was an envelope. Inside, beneath the paper, a piece of card acted as a supporting layer. The card helped support the sheet during movement, whereas the envelope enclosed the package. Neither component should be confused with the boards used earlier to apply pressure. On the drawing, the first arrow points to the outside covering and the second to the supporting layer beneath the paper. In actual collections the materials and treatment would be selected for the particular object and its condition. The team concluded by discussing what the observations could show. A change in colour or flexibility can be recorded, but a small teaching comparison cannot by itself establish the cause of every change. Additional controlled work would be needed before generalising from these samples. Keeping the same description method and image scale helps make observations comparable, while careful handling reduces the chance of creating new damage during inspection. Finally, the students entered the date of each inspection alongside the sample identifier. That record made it possible to follow the sequence of observations without relying on memory. The class kept the two sample histories separate and noted both the limits of the comparison and the practical reason for using each support.

items.stem: (31) Damage can be caused by water in the form of ______.
items.why: Paper can be damaged by moisture 给出原因。
inspected each sheet with a magnifier 指明工具。
干燥储存的样本记录 colour。
加湿储存的样本记录 flexibility。

items.stem: (35) The team avoided direct ______ on the paper.
items.why: avoided direct sunlight on the paper 指明避免的光照。

items.stem: (36) A consistent ______ beside each sheet provides a reference for dimensions.
items.why: used a consistent scale beside each sheet 作为比较参照。

items.stem: (37) After inspection, place the sheet between ______.
items.why: the sheet was placed between boards，随后施加压力。

items.stem: (38) After pressure, store the sheet in a ______.
items.why: After this stage, the sheet was stored in a folder，最后放入文件夹。
The outer cover was an envelope，外层是信封。
a piece of card acted as a supporting layer，纸板提供支撑。
